messages:
julie: FYI customer AcmeCorp (acct: acme-42) reporting a spike in 429s on their Dedicated pool dp-712 after this morning's billing cutover. They say errors started ~09:15 UTC, ~5% of requests returning 429 or auth failures. Can we triage?
kevin: Which 429 are they seeing — gateway rate limit or our reserved-pool enforcement? Any sample responses/logs?
nate: I'm oncall, looking now. Julie can you paste a sample response and approximate qps pattern?
julie: sample from customer app: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "detail": "reserved_pool_quota_exhausted dp-712",
  "retry_after": 3
}
```
They also saw intermittent 401s with billing service returning 402 on token check. Traffic pattern: steady 200 qps, spikes to 600 qps in bursts for ~15s every 3 minutes.
samir: dp-712 is a Dedicated instance with committed throughput 400 qps and burst window 30s allowed. If they're spiking to 600 qps often the reserved pool will hit the hard cap. Are they using streaming responses or many parallel short requests?
julie: their app uses 1-2 token streaming responses but parallelism is high: 300 concurrent connections during spikes.
kevin: That combination will absolutely blow past the 400 sustained + 30s burst margin. Two questions: did the billing cutover change any allocation keys or per-account quota mapping?
billing-bot: billing-service: cutover to v2 meter on acme-42 completed at 09:05 UTC. No change to committed throughput metadata.
maria: I was on the ACME call. They mentioned their account id in the request header changed (we issued a new client-id at cutover). Might be hitting a different routing path that bypasses existing reserved pool mapping.
nate: Good lead. Can ops check the customer-id -> reserved-pool mapping for dp-712, specifically the client-id header mapping? Also check gateway logs for auth path differences.
ops-oncall: Pulling logs for client-id header x-client-id: acme-v2-019. Quick grep shows some requests hitting route /v2/gen and a few routed to fallback pool f-pool-9 between 09:12–09:20.
samir: If some traffic landed on fallback pool that has much lower capacity, that explains the rapid 429s. Why would routing change? Two possibilities: (1) header value not recognized so smart-routing picked default, or (2) reserved pool controller temporarily removed dp-712 endpoints during deployment.
kevin: Can we repro locally by replaying their spike with x-client-id: acme-v2-019 and observe which pool is selected? julie can you share a small repro curl?
julie: repro curl (sanitized):
```
for i in {1..700}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Id: acme-v2-019" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done; wait
```
kevin: Running a scaled replay in staging now against a traffic generator. If routing is misaligned we'll see requests to f-pool-9 in traces. Sharing a short command to fetch pool selection from the gateway logs: 
```
jq -r 'select(.client_id=="acme-v2-019") | .pool_selected' /var/log/gateway/requests-*.ndjson | sort | uniq -c
```
nate: Also check reserved-pool controller logs around 09:00–09:10 for any endpoint churn: `/var/log/reservedpool/controller.log` grep for dp-712.
ops-oncall: Controller logs show a rolling config refresh at 09:04 where dp-712 had an endpoint marked drained for 40s due to healthcheck flapping. That could briefly reduce available capacity.
samir: So two contributors: config refresh/healthcheck caused transient capacity drop, and new client-id routing caused some percent to go to fallback pool. Combined, bursts exceeded remaining headroom and produced 429s.
maria: ACME is worried about SLA hit. They need mitigation ASAP — can we bump temporary burst allowance or map acme-v2-019 explicitly to dp-712?
kevin: We can add a hotfix to routing rules to bind acme-v2-019 -> dp-712; changing pool mapping is quick. For burst allowance, we can adjust controller to allow +200 qps for next 30 minutes to catch up. Both ops and infra approvals required.
nate: I'll approve emergency mapping plus temporary margin. Samir, can you push mapping and increase burst window while you fix the healthcheck flapping?
samir: On it. I'll: 1) bind x-client-id acme-v2-019 -> dp-712, 2) increase burst ceiling to 600 qps for 30m, 3) investigate healthchecks. Pushing change in 2 mins.
ops-oncall: Changes applied: mapping added, burst_ceiling updated. Monitoring now.
kevin: Julie, can you confirm with ACME if errors drop?
julie: I told them we've applied fixes, they're running tests now. They say 429s dropped to near 0 within 40s. Thank you.
maria: I'll schedule a post-mortem with ACME and include: (a) why client-id changed at cutover, (b) routing verification as part of billing cutovers, (c) add automated check that mapping exists after account-id rotations.
nate: Action items captured: samir investigate healthcheck flaps + root cause, kevin add a pre-cutover mapping verification checklist, devex to update cutover runbook. I'll keep this thread open until follow-up doc posted.
julie: closing loop for now — customer back to normal. Will follow up with PM and ACME notes. :white_check_mark:
